overall: The AG found no violation on the executive session and June 4 discussion allegations, but found the April 30, 2012 notice violated the law for omitting any mention of open session, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered executive session for an improper purpose at its April 30, 2012 meeting, whose notice cited personnel matters.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board never entered into executive session during its April 30, 2012 meeting, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered an improper executive session at its May 17, 2012 meeting, which was noticed under complaint-against-individual purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law because the Board did not meet on May 17, 2012.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed and acted on an item not listed on the June 4, 2012 meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board's discussion during the June 4, 2012 meeting concerned the posted, anticipated agenda item, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not raised by complainant: the AG noted the April 30, 2012 notice said the meeting would be entirely in executive session and omitted that an open session would occur.
allegations.key_passage: The notice therefore did not comply with the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation
